speaker: Doctor
text: I see you have a yellowish tint to your skin and eyes, along with some agitation. To help me understand what's causing this, can you tell me if you've experienced any abdominal pain, fever, or changes in your urine or stool color recently?

speaker: Patient
text: 20-year-old male. The patient was previously healthy and has been brought to the emergency department due to agitation over the past 24 hours. Family members have noticed a yellowish coloring of his skin and eyes over the past week. The patient has a history of occasional cocaine and ecstasy use, and drinks alcohol socially on weekends. The patient also admits to high-risk sexual behaviors without using appropriate protection.

speaker: Doctor
text: Given your history of high-risk sexual behavior and recent substance use, I need to rule out acute hepatitis. Have you noticed any dark, tea-colored urine or pale, clay-colored stools over the past week?

speaker: Doctor
text: To further narrow down the cause, have you experienced any nausea, vomiting, or loss of appetite recently? Also, do you have any pain or tenderness in the upper right side of your abdomen?

speaker: Patient
text: Past medical history: No significant past medical history. Social history: Occasional use of cocaine and ecstasy. Social alcohol consumption (about 20 g on weekends).

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Liver Function Panel: Bilirubin 25 mg/dL (elevated), AST 600 IU/L (elevated), ALT 650 IU/L (elevated), TP Activity < 40% (reduced), INR 1.5 (elevated). Hepatitis A, B, C Serology: NORMAL READINGS. Urine Drug Screen: NORMAL READINGS.

speaker: Doctor
text: Your lab results show severe liver dysfunction with markedly elevated bilirubin and enzymes, but negative hepatitis serologies. Since common viral causes are ruled out, have you recently taken any new medications, supplements, or herbal remedies?

speaker: Patient
text: The patient shows signs of psychomotor agitation and confusion. No other symptoms provided.

speaker: Doctor
text: Given the negative viral hepatitis and drug screens, I need to consider autoimmune or metabolic causes. Do you have any personal or family history of autoimmune diseases, or have you noticed any joint pains or rashes?

speaker: Patient
text: The patient shows signs of psychomotor agitation and confusion. No other symptoms provided.

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Autoimmune Hepatitis Panel: NORMAL READINGS. Ceruloplasmin: 25 mg/dL (low). Acetaminophen Level: 45 mcg/mL (therapeutic/non-toxic).

speaker: Doctor
text: The low ceruloplasmin level is highly suggestive of Wilson's disease, which can present with acute liver failure and neuropsychiatric symptoms. I need to confirm the diagnosis by looking for increased copper excretion. REQUEST TEST: 24-Hour_Urine_Copper

speaker: Doctor
text: The elevated 24-hour urine copper confirms the diagnosis of Wilson's disease. DIAGNOSIS READY: Wilson's disease
